A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiSS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v11 reports original synthetic adaptation experiments, language benchmark results, convergence analyses, and efficiency measurements, plus RWKV7 results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v12 retains original language, synthetic, and efficiency results, including appendix experiments. These establish original empirical content independently of the ambiguous attribution of its new vision table.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the written MiSSe aggregation from summation within r blocks of length g to aggregation of g slices of length r, changing coordinate grouping. Ordinary MiSS remains unchanged. Conflicting retained prose and the x^(g) summand under an i-indexed sum leave the implementation used for results unclear.

E1.justification: v12 Table 6 extends reported evaluation beyond language and synthetic regression to seven image tasks and UCF101, Kinetics, and HMDB video tasks. Existing coverage is retained. The caption attributes results to SliceFine, so this establishes expanded reported coverage without establishing that all these experiments were newly conducted.

E2.justification: The LLaMA2-7B convergence comparison expands from LoRA and MiSS in v11 Figure 4 to LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA, and MiSS in v12 Figure 5. DoRA and PiSSA appeared elsewhere previously but are newly included in this comparison. Retained language tables preserve their comparator sets.

E3.justification: v12 adds cross-task Avg metrics to the language tables and switches the Pareto memory objective from average reserved memory to peak memory; both memory measurements were already tabulated. Appendix B identifies ViT-Base-Patch16-224 for the added image evaluation. Retained language and synthetic settings are unchanged where documented.

E4.justification: The convergence analysis is revised with additional DoRA and PiSSA trajectories and different displayed token/time horizons. The Pareto analysis uses a different memory objective and revised frontiers. The rank sensitivity study, initial-gradient analysis, and synthetic adaptation analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: GLUE retains identical uncertainty reporting and three-seed information. Both versions retain the discrepancy between three independent runs in the NLG table caption and two seeds in its setup prose. Synthetic seed 43 is unchanged, and no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v12 adds substantial cross-domain results in Table 6, including MiSS averages of 88.02 for images and 72.96 for video, and adds aggregate language scores. The convergence trajectories and Pareto frontiers also change; the token plot now extends to approximately 0.025 billion rather than 0.20 billion tokens. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains. Existing per-task language scores, rank results, RWKV7 results, and the Llama-3.2-3B measurement table are retained.

T1.justification: v12 revises the formal input-partition and aggregation definitions and expands the complexity analysis in Section 4.3 with parameter/FLOP expressions for additional methods and a two-stage computational decomposition. MiSSe's rewritten total complexity is algebraically equivalent to its earlier bound. The existing low-rank argument is retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction changes MiSSe from a mathematically equivalent formulation of MiSS to an alternative design preserving parameter sharing through input aggregation. This narrows the equivalence claim. The abstract, principal contribution statements, and conclusion retain the central performance-memory-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 explains why fewer trainable parameters need not reduce computation and locates MiSSe's advantage in input transformation rather than output projection. v12 also treats non-textual applicability as empirically supported, replacing v11's speculative multimodal-applicability paragraph in Section 7. Existing convergence and rank interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v12 adds the ViT-Base-Patch16-224 architecture disclosure but removes v11's OpenCompass and MATH 5-shot evaluation footnote. This is lost documentation, not evidence that prompting changed. Language hyperparameters, preprocessing descriptions, hardware information, synthetic settings, and code-access links are otherwise retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v12 adds citations to LoRA-FA and SliceFine. LoRA-FA joins the introduction's methodological motivation and the expanded complexity comparison; SliceFine is credited for the vision results. Existing related-work coverage and overall positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v12 combines the main NLU/NLG discussion into Section 5.1, rewrites its result summaries, and moves setup paragraphs to a new Appendix B. It adds an efficiency subsection, revises headings, and adds a correspondence footnote. Most introductory, related-work, methodological, and concluding prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The presentation is substantially revised: two expanded complexity tables replace the earlier compact table, a vision table and Avg columns are added, and both convergence and Pareto figures are redrawn with changed axes and legends. The convergence figure is enlarged and moved to the appendix. Boxed introductory statements and rearranged tables further change the layout.

improvement.justification: v12 broadens reported coverage, expands convergence comparisons, and explains computational costs more explicitly. However, the new vision evidence has ambiguous provenance and sparse settings; Table 6 reports a full-tuning video average of 74.99 although its three entries average 71.11. The revised aggregation remains internally inconsistent, changed convergence curves lack corresponding protocol explanations, and the 5-shot disclosure disappears. These benefits and evidential weaknesses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
